11:06 < jal0> hey prk, sorry, must of missed you
11:16 -!- prk_away is now known as prk
11:16 < prk> hi jal0!
11:16 < jal0> hey prk
11:16 < jal0> how things going
11:17 < prk> I wanted you to ask a question
11:17 < jal0> ok shoot, i try my best ;)
11:18 < prk> I have been looking the execptions code for vr41xx
11:19 < prk> and I have seen that the cvs (linux-mips.org) 2.4 version uses a generic r4000 exception vector for the tlb refill one
11:19 < jal0> yeap
11:20 < prk> that is doing something like:
11:20 < prk> mtc0    k1, CP0_ENTRYLO1
11:20 < prk> b 1f
11:21 < prk> tlbwr
11:21 < prk> 1: nop
11:21 < prk> eret
11:22 < prk> and my vr manual says that I need 2 instructions betwen a mtc0 and tlbwr (coprocesor hazard)
11:23 < prk> I don't have much idea about mips assembler... but i feel that this except vector doesnt do that, right?
11:23 < jal0> hang on let me grap my manual
11:26 < jal0> ok, you question is?
11:27 < prk> is that code doing 2 instructions betwen mtc0 and tlbwr?
11:28 < jal0> nope.
11:29 < jal0> whats the instuction before the mtc0
11:29 < jal0> the # of required instruction is based on the operation being done
11:31 < prk> is a slr to adapt some register contents to the cp0 entrylo and entryhi
11:34 < prk> following the manual, the number of instructions needed are computed with (destination hazard)-(source hazard+1)
11:34 < jal0> but those instruction are the count before the next mtc0 and mfc0 not the tlbwr
11:36 < prk> I don't know :)
11:37 < jal0> p. 421 of the Vr4100 Series Arch. manual
11:39 < prk> ...reading...
11:43 < prk> ok, now I have to see what is my source and what is my destination :)
11:46 < prk> mtc0 is the "destination" instruction with 5 nr of cycles
11:47 < prk> better, the destination is the CP0_entryLO1
11:48 < prk> and I use tlbrwr, with cp0_entrylo1 as source
11:48 < prk> with 2 nr of cycles
11:48 < jal0> 2 instruction must follow tlbrwr
11:50 < prk> and 2 ahead too?
11:51 < prk> I mean, I'm computing the number of instructions betwen mtc0 and tlbwr
11:51 < jal0> it would seem, but not sure what the 'b 1f' is
11:52 < jal0> that looks like a asm macro not an instruction
11:52 < prk> branch 1 foward. the next 1:
11:54 < jal0> so the two instructions requirement is made, the branch,and the nop, while the tlbwr is que'ed in the instruction pipeline
11:55 < jal0> and is executed 3rd
11:56 < prk> I don't know what i can call a "instruction" with the delay slots in mips :)
11:59 < jal0> yeah that was new to me also, i mainly work with simpler mcu's at work
11:59 < prk> I tought that when theres a jump or a branch the processor begins to execute the next instruction, just in case that the branch don't "jump"
12:01 < jal0> dosn't execute it unless there is 'no' jump. if there is, then the instruction is flushed.
12:02 < jal0> btw: don't take what i say here as hard fact, i'm just learning this stuff also :)
12:02 < prk> I don't get it
12:03 < prk> oh, wait
12:04 < jal0> A good book for introduction to the mips arch. is 'See Mips RUN' it has been invaluable duing my work with the linux4BE.
12:06 < prk> it is a "hard" branch so, it doesn't have sense to execute the "next" instruction, so it begin execution of the nop instruction... so we have 2 instructions before tlbwr
12:07 < prk> no, because then the tlbrw doesn't execute at all
12:07 < prk> conclusion: I need "see mips run"
12:08 < jal0> i wonder what instruction the assembler will produce for the 'b 1f'?
12:09 < jal0> you on a linux or windows box?
12:10 < prk> just looking at the disasembled code
12:10 < prk> it is simply a branch to the location of the nop
12:11 < prk> 800022c4:       10000001        b       800022cc <except_vec0_r4000+0x4c> 
12:11 < prk> 800022c8:       42000006        tlbwr 
12:11 < prk> 800022cc:       00000000        nop 
12:12 < prk> 800022d0:       42000018        eret 
12:15 < jal0> beq s,t,p
12:15 < prk> and i feel that we have the same betwen tlbrw and eret :(
12:16 < jal0> so the tlbrw is executed before the branch
12:18 < prk> you say that 10000001 is beq?
12:18 < jal0> yeap
12:19 < jal0> beq 0,0,1
12:20 < jal0> or beq zero,zero,0x01
12:21 < prk> aha
12:22 < jal0> of course you could try replacing the 'b 1f' instruction with it and decompiling again to verify
12:27 < prk> how I put the 0 register in assembly, "zero" is defined?
12:28 < jal0> i believe, or just put 0 directly
12:29 < jal0> in your dism, do a grep, maybe its used somewhere else
12:30 < prk> #define zero $0
12:30 < jal0> ahaa
12:31 < prk> just the same
12:31 < prk> what you said
12:31 < jal0> :)
12:32 < jal0> i'm pretty good with coverting machine code. i wrote a dissembler for mips ;)
12:33 < prk> but i don't get how much instructions "are" executed "betwen"
12:33 < prk> sure it was a good work :)
12:34 < jal0> have you tried asking on #mipslinux
12:34 < prk> yea, but it seems the gurus are on holidays :)
12:34 < jal0> ;) ... figures

12:36 < prk> i haven't looked at the linux-vr.org code
12:39 < prk> guess what?
12:39 < jal0> ?
12:40 < prk> they put 2 nops!

12:41 < prk> and no branch
